title: Cache upgrade crashes on startup
reason: The diagnosis correctly identifies the cache (Redis) as the broken part, describes a crash/restart loop, and attributes it to the Redis 7.5 upgrade rejecting an obsolete config directive.
root_cause: The Redis 7.5 container crashes on startup because its configuration file /etc/redis/redis.conf contains the directive 'maxmemory-policy' which Redis 7.5 does not recognize, causing a continuous restart loop that makes the cache unavailable to the API.
truth: A deploy upgraded Redis from 7.4 to 7.5; the new version refuses to start because the existing redis.conf uses a removed configuration directive, so the cache container crashes in a restart loop and the API cannot reach it.
check_first: Inspect the API container's logs and status (e.g., docker logs <api_container> or pod status).
